strengths: Novel problem identification with strong empirical evidence: Quantifies capability degradation as a real phenomenon (62.33%/55.80% R@1 vs 100% for foundation model on solvable subsets)
Well-motivated solution design: Diagnose-generate-refine pipeline strategically targets decision boundaries rather than indiscriminate scaling, demonstrated by Random Mining comparison
Strong experimental results: Achieves SOTA on CIRR (55.52% R@1 vs 53.64% for CIR-LVLM) and FashionIQ (57.04% avg R@10), with substantial improvements over baseline (8.38% and 7.16% respectively)
Comprehensive ablation studies: Progressive validation (Table 4) and Random Mining baseline (Table 3) clearly demonstrate the contribution of each component with proper statistical reporting
Generalizability across model backbones: Validated effectiveness on both Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B, showing the approach works even with stronger foundation models
Data efficiency: Focused diagnosis demonstrates superior efficiency compared to blind synthesis, maximizing gradient signal per synthetic triplet
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Individual components are well-established (CoT prompting, VQA filtering, triplet loss, contrastive learning); grouped contrastive refinement is a straightforward batching strategy without fundamental innovation

Critical implementation details missing for reproducibility: Intent Decomposition & Verification procedures lack specificity; exact prompts, minimal edit constraints, VQA confidence thresholds, and top-K selection values not provided; code not available despite reliance on MLLM prompting quality

Insufficient analysis of method mechanics: No reporting of VQA filtering rates to assess quality control effectiveness; missing sensitivity analysis for prompt variations, hyperparameter K, or quality thresholds; no systematic failure case analysis beyond 2 qualitative examples

Computational cost unaddressed: Foundation model must be run for every training instance (mining + generation + verification); no quantification of training time, resource overhead, or FLOPs compared to baseline—critical for practical applicability

Narrow evaluation scope: Only two closely related datasets (fashion e-commerce and NLVR2-derived); no evaluation on other compositional reasoning tasks; generalization to significantly different domains unclear; model-agnostic claim only validated on Qwen family

Incomplete comparative analysis: No investigation of whether capability degradation exists in other MLLM adaptations (CIR-LVLM, etc.); missing VQA-based retrieval vs embedding-based tradeoff comparison; no comparison with alternative self-improvement strategies

Experimental design concerns: Inconsistent hyperparameters across datasets without justification; arbitrary 'Avg.' metric definition; only 4 random seeds for Random Mining; no statistical significance testing for main results; missing ablations on loss weight sensitivity
Overstated claims: 'Model-agnostic' claim unsupported (Qwen variants only); 'paradigm conflict' never formally defined; applicability beyond retrieval tasks unexplored

strengths: Clear and well-motivated identification of capability degradation phenomenon with strong empirical evidence (Figure 1: 62.33% vs. 100% R@1)
Comprehensive experimental validation including thorough ablations, cross-backbone generalization, and cross-model transfer studies demonstrating model-agnostic applicability
Strong empirical results achieving state-of-the-art on CIRR (+8.38% R@1) and FashionIQ (+7.16% avg R@10) with consistent improvements
Practical and efficient framework with reasonable one-time offline synthesis cost (10-14h) and comparable refinement training time
Extensive qualitative analysis including failure case studies, triplet synthesis visualizations, and interpretable examples demonstrating what the model learns
Thorough supplementary material with prompt details, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, computational breakdowns, and reproducibility information
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: combines existing techniques (self-guided mining, CoT generation, VQA filtering, triplet loss) without significant algorithmic innovation

Shallow theoretical understanding of capability degradation: identifies the phenomenon but doesn't explain the underlying mechanism (representation collapse, loss mismatch, etc.). Table 8 shows increasing capacity worsens performance but lacks mechanistic analysis
Narrow experimental scope: evaluation limited to two CIR datasets in similar domains (fashion/open-domain). No evidence of generalization to other retrieval tasks or domains

Data quality and reliability concerns: VQA-based filtering achieves only 92% accuracy (~8% noise), assumption that foundation model F always provides correct reasoning contradicted by Section 8.3 failure analysis showing F has residual weaknesses
Heavy reliance on prompt engineering with reproducibility concerns: code link redacted, results likely sensitive to prompt wording variations, unclear how to adapt to different MLLM versions
Incomplete analysis of when/why approach fails: Section 8.3 identifies ambiguous instructions and spatial reasoning challenges with no proposed solutions, suggesting fundamental limitations
Incremental performance gains (7-8% on R@1) may not justify the added complexity of four-stage pipeline and offline data synthesis

Unresolved methodological questions: unclear if grouped contrastive strategy risks model preferring corrected variants on all data, minimal edit principle enforced only via prompting without systematic verification
